summary: Phase 1 is a single repository-ready authority-boundary increment for recoverable free-form changes between workflow milestones. It separates exact first-parent historical milestone proof from current baseline reconciliation; routes governing planning-document drift through restoration or fresh owning authority; adds replay-safe missing-proof recovery and stale baseline-interface refresh; preserves human and no-wait authority distinctions; updates contracts, schemas, skills, maintained documentation, and tracked dist/; and verifies document, implementation, adoption, restore, stale-decision, rewrite, and final-completion journeys. The broad phase is intentionally atomic because partial proof, reconciliation, or recovery changes would leave unusable or unsafe intermediate states. Principal implementation risks are retroactive authorization of descendants, stale decisions across replaced history, unreviewed plan bytes reaching successors, revival of pre-recovery authority, stale tracked release payloads, and status/mutation disagreement; the design pins exact candidate selection, first-parent continuity, authority cutoffs, shared race-closing proof, governing-drift priority, payload regeneration, and deep verification to address them. The first independent review identified the missing tracked-release refresh; it was accepted and added. Fresh independent counter-review and constitution review then completed with no findings. Approval authorizes these exact design bytes and their task-local design milestone commit; it does not itself authorize implementation code.
